newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices regain some lost ground in edgy market.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices regain some lost ground in edgy market.

text.p: Oil prices regained some lost ground on Thursday but the market was still reeling from the previous day's steep decline that followed the resumption of Iraqi crude flows.

January futures of world benchmark Brent Blend crude traded 35 cents higher at $22.50 a barrel at 1507 GMT, having earlier scrambled to an intra-day high of $22.68. Crude still had some way to go to make up for the $2 a barrel it has lost since last week.
A late sell-off largely led by investment funds on Wednesday alone shaved $1.14 a barrel off the price of a barrel of crude but brokers believe the market is not yet heavily oversold.
"A lot of yesterday was closing out long positions. I don't think many people got a chance to go short," said a futures broker, expecting further declines after an initial bounce.

"I am not convinced," said another futures trader of Thurdsay's early gains. "It really depends how much length is left in the market. If there's still some length, there's still potential for further falls."

Front-month Brent crude futures have not traded below $22 a barrel since September, when the market was anticipating the start of the much-delayed resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the U.N. partial sales plan.
Oil prices soared in October to $25.06 a barrel, their highest level since the Gulf crisis of August 1990, when Iraq invaded Kuwait and provoked the United Nations into imposing sanctions.

Under the U.N.-Iraq deal concluded in May, Baghdad will be allowed oil sales worth $2.0 billion over six months to buy food and medicines. The first oil flow began on Thursday but none of the crude has left the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan yet.
Turkey said the first cargo of Iraqi crude would load on Friday for transport to a Turkish refinery.

"Clearly a bearish tone has set in now and we wait for clear and sustained signs of strength, such as buying extremes before we would recommend any buying," said MeesPierson Derivatives in their daily report.

The resumed oil flow from Iraq through its trans-Turkey pipeline followed the release late on Tuesday of U.S. weekly stock data which showed that the recent shortfall in heating oil, which had underpinned the market, was beginning to ease.
"The bears have been smelling blood in the past few days and it's not over yet, even if yesterday's move was rather sharp," said brokerage GNI in a report. Crude oil prices in dollars per barrel:
